name: Question 11
problem:
Consider the orthogonal set $U$ below. By adding a new vector $x=[{x}_{1},\,{x}_{2},\,{x}_{3}]^{T},$ extend the set so that it forms an orthogonal basis of ${R}^{3}.$ What is the value of $\frac{{x}_{1}}{{x}_{2}}?$

$$
U={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}
$$
worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $U$ as ${u}_{1},\,{u}_{2}.$ To extend the given set to an orthogonal basis of ${R}^{3}$, we need to find a third vector $x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]$ such that

$$
{\begin{aligned}{u}_{1}\cdot x=0 \\ {u}_{2}\cdot x=0\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=0 \\ 2{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we consider the augmented matrix $M$ of the system above and reduce it to its row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 2 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 8 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns ($1$st and $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we get ${x}_{2}=\frac{1}{4}{x}_{3}.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-3(\frac{1}{4}{x}_{3})+2{x}_{3}=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-\frac{5}{4}{x}_{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{5}{4}{x}_{3} \\ \frac{1}{4}{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Setting ${x}_{3}=4,$ we obtain the vector 

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 1 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, an orthogonal basis of ${R}^{3}$ is

$$
{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 1 \\ 4\end{aligned}]}.
$$

Finally, $\frac{{x}_{1}}{{x}_{2}}=\frac{-5}{1}=-5.$

EXPLANATION

Let's denote the vectors of U as u1,u2. To extend the given set to an orthogonal basis of R3, we need to find a third vector x=[x1x2x3] such that

{u1⋅x=0u2⋅x=0⟹{x1−3x2+2x3=02x1+2x2+2x3=0.

Now, we consider the augmented matrix M of the system above and reduce it to its row echelon form, as follows:

M=[1−3202220]R1:=R2−2R1∼[1−32008−20]

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (1st and 2nd). Thus, x3 is a free variable. From the second equation, we get x2=14x3. Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

x1−3(14x3)+2x3=0⟹x1=−54x3.

So, the general solution is [−54x314x3x3],x3∈R.

Setting x3=4, we obtain the vector

x=[−514].

Therefore, an orthogonal basis of R3 is {[1−32],[222],[−514]}.

Finally, x1x2=−51=−5.
